bson-decimal128/decimal128.md.reason: Deterministic Decimal128 interchange and exact numeric behavior are covered by the exact-value unit vectors.

bson-objectid/objectid.md.reason: Deterministic runtime vectors cover timestamps 0x00000000, 0x7fffffff, 0x80000000, and 0xffffffff as unsigned big-endian values.
A deterministic generator vector covers the 24-bit counter rollover from 0xffffff to zero.
The generator does not yet detect a fork or equivalent process-identity change and regenerate its five-byte process-unique value.

collation/collation.md.reason: Command builders preserve collation documents and enforce the negotiated unacknowledged-write restrictions.

compression/OP_COMPRESSED.md.reason: The five pinned URI-option cases and deterministic programmatic vectors cover ordered compressors, unknown-name warnings, defaults, and every zlib compression level from -1 through 9.
Exact vectors cover compressor ID 2 and every supported zlib compression level, while invalid input returns a structured protocol failure.
Byte-exact vectors cover opcode 2012, the original opcode, the header-excluding uncompressed size, compressor ID, and compression failures.

Deterministic vectors select each response provider by envelope ID, accept ordinary or compressed replies including the initial hello, and reject unknown IDs, malformed sizes, oversized frames, and provider failures.

Each connection advertises only available configured compressors in client order, selects the first client-preferred overlap, tolerates no overlap, and does not renegotiate after its initial handshake.
The exact case-insensitive command matrix keeps hello, legacy hello, authentication, user-management, and copydb authentication commands uncompressed while allowing ordinary commands.
Every sharded compatibility row enables zlib on the public client before exercising commands, indexes, sessions, and transactions through a real mongos.
Every standalone and replica-set compatibility row enables zlib before a public-client ping against its pinned live MongoDB server.
An exact raw Snappy vector covers compressor ID 1 and a TCP integration round trip verifies negotiated OP_COMPRESSED framing.
Public-client integration cases omit unavailable Snappy and Zstandard providers from the handshake and expose one credential-free warning for each configured codec.
An exact Zstandard frame vector covers compressor ID 3 and a TCP integration round trip verifies negotiated OP_COMPRESSED framing.

dbref/dbref.md.reason: The driver preserves DBRef-shaped BSON documents but exposes no class-style DBRef abstraction, so applicability needs an explicit classification.

enumerate-collections/enumerate-collecti.reason: Deterministic admin and topology vectors verify primary selection plus standalone, replica-set primary, directly connected replica-set secondary, and mongos routing.

enumerate-databases/enumerate-databases..reason: Deterministic admin and topology vectors verify primary selection plus standalone, replica-set primary, directly connected replica-set secondary, and mongos routing.

extended-json/extended-json.md.reason: Canonical and relaxed Extended JSON conversion is covered by deterministic ordered-value unit vectors.

find_getmore_killcursors_commands/find_g.reason: Find, getMore, killCursors, exhaustion, and cleanup are covered at deterministic command and transport boundaries.

gridfs/gridfs-spec.md.reason: Deterministic public and unified-adapter vectors cover immutable bucket names, chunk sizes, concerns, preferences, timeouts, and the disableMD5 compatibility no-op without database I/O.
The first bucket write lazily compares and creates both required indexes, while an empty upload stores one zero-length files document and no chunks.
Upload-stream vectors cover exact chunk boundaries, final partial chunks, per-file overrides, metadata, custom ids, terminal close, and structured write failures without orphan cleanup.
Abort removes written chunks, omits the files document, closes the stream, rejects later writes, and preserves a cleanup failure.
Readable-source uploads preserve caller ownership and apply one timeout context across index discovery, chunk writes, and the final files insert.
Download streams cover exact bytes, bounded reads, seek and tell, zero-length files, numeric field variants, missing files, and required chunk ordering and length validation.
Destination-copy vectors preserve exact byte order and the first structured read, write, or cleanup failure without closing the caller-owned destination.
Filename downloads select positive revisions oldest-first and negative revisions newest-first and distinguish a missing filename from an out-of-range revision.
Named destination-copy vectors select the requested revision and share one timeout across lookup and chunks without closing the caller-owned destination.
Deletion vectors remove the files document before chunks, optionally clean orphan chunks, and return the GridFS not-found error for a missing file.
Filename deletion discovers every revision id, removes only those files before their chunks, and returns the GridFS not-found error when no revision exists.
Find returns a cursor-like iterable and forwards the filter, all GridFS find options, concerns, preference, and the cursor-lifetime timeout without filter validation.
Rename-by-id changes only the selected files document filename and returns the GridFS not-found error when the id is absent.
Rename-by-name changes every matching revision and no other files and returns the GridFS not-found error when the filename is absent.
Bucket drop removes only the configured files collection and then chunks collection under one operation timeout and stops on the first failure.

ocsp-support/ocsp-support.md.reason: LuaSec 1.3 does not expose certificate revocation, OCSP stapling, or OCSP endpoint verification, and this driver will not add a separate OCSP implementation.

polling-srv-records-for-mongos-discovery.reason: All thirteen prose polling cases run against deterministic DNS, clock, and topology adapters.

server_write_commands/server_write_comma.reason: Insert, update, delete, ordered batching, and acknowledged error shapes are covered by deterministic command vectors.

socks5-support/socks5.md.reason: SOCKS5 proxy options and transport behavior remain a declared post-v1 runtime-adapter feature.
